title: Car Pooling
statement: A car drives in one direction with a fixed seat capacity. Each trip [passengers, pickup, dropoff] boards at the pickup point and leaves at the dropoff point. Return True if the car never exceeds its capacity.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(10)
    t = []
    for _ in range(10000):
        a = r.randint(0, 990)
        t.append([r.randint(1, 3), a, a + r.randint(1, 9)])
    return [t, 100]

hints.1_question: You only care about how many passengers are in the car at each location. What changes at a pickup? At a dropoff?
hints.2_nudge: Mark +passengers at the pickup and -passengers at the dropoff, then sweep left to right keeping a running total.
hints.3_big_hint: diff[from] += num; diff[to] -= num. Sweep with a running sum; if it ever exceeds capacity return False. Drop-off at x frees the seats before a pickup at x.

known_bugs.name: treats the dropoff point as still occupied
known_bugs.followup: Passengers get off at their dropoff location. If someone else boards at that same location, are the seats free?

known_bugs.name: rejects when exactly full (>= instead of >)
known_bugs.followup: If the car has 2 seats and 2 passengers, is that over capacity?

known_bugs.name: only checks each trip on its own
known_bugs.code:
def carPooling(trips, capacity):
    return all(t[0] <= capacity for t in trips)
known_bugs.followup: What if two trips overlap in time? Does checking trips one by one capture the total on board?

complexity.time: O(n + L) where L = last location
followups: What if locations go up to 10^9? How would you adapt without allocating a huge array?
How does the sweep-line version with sorted events compare?
